head_commit.message:
fix(dunning-v2): match the Day-10 lockout allow-list on full route prefixes, per-class AST route inventory

Squash of PR #523 (feat/dun-1a-lockout-allowlist-route-table), 3 commits onto main @ 5076a07a:
- cbb0496 fix(dunning-v2): match the lockout allow-list on full route prefixes, not segment position
- 0e37ee5 test(dunning-v2): build the lockout route inventory from the TS AST, per controller class
- 5b74043 test(dunning-v2): condense route-table spec prose to fit the R100.A3 LOC cap

Fixes two live security findings against the Day-10 lockout guard (dunning-lockout.guard.ts):
- Google OAuth routes (scheduling/auth/google/initiate, /callback) were wrongly reachable while a
  coach's account is locked -- now correctly LOCKED.
- v1 coach billing routes (coach/me/billing, coach/me/billing/portal-session) were wrongly locked,
  blocking a coach's own payment-recovery path -- now correctly ALLOWED.
Also corrects two provenance comments (LandingPagePublicController naming; /auth/logout and
/auth/refresh don't exist, the real mounted route is /auth/extension/refresh) and replaces the
prior file-level route inventory test with a real TypeScript-compiler-AST-based, per-controller-class
inventory (366 lines, 25 tests) that independently attributes all 712 routes across 171 controller
classes -- closing the exact "a new controller can silently inherit an exemption" gap the prior
file-level test could not see.

## R138 Decision Gate

1. Musk's algorithm (question requirements / delete / simplify / accelerate / automate): The
   requirement -- an allow-list guard must key off the actual mounted route, not an incidental
   file-scan artifact -- was already correct; the bug was in matching logic (segment-position instead
   of full-prefix) and in the test's ability to see per-class attribution. No requirement was added,
   deleted, or gold-plated; the fix is the minimal correct match plus a test that can actually catch
   regressions of this class going forward.
2. Hyperscaler practice: Route-table-driven authorization tests validated by an AST walk (not a
   regex/file heuristic) is standard practice for any multi-tenant SaaS backend with a large,
   fast-growing controller surface (171 classes here) -- this brings the codebase in line with that.
3. Good-without-bad: The fix closes a real security bypass (locked-out coach could still reach Google
   OAuth) and a real support/product issue (locked-out coach could not reach billing self-service) with
   zero net-new banned casts, LOC within the R100.A3 400-line cap (399 net), and a test:src ratio well
   above the R74/R100.A1 floor. No regression found by two independent fresh auditors across 4 combined
   audit passes (correctness/security lens + test-quality/doctrine lens), each reproducing every claim
   from scratch via their own methods.
4. Root cause: The root cause was a heuristic (second-path-segment matching) standing in for the actual
   contract (full mounted route prefix), compounded by a test suite that scanned files rather than
   classes and so could not see the heuristic's blind spots. Both are fixed at the root, not patched
   around: the guard now matches full normalized prefixes, and the test now walks the real AST per
   class, independently re-verified working against real production source (not just fixtures) by both
   auditors via their own from-scratch controller-append mutations.

## Audit trail
Two independent, fresh-context, zero-cross-context auditors (Lens A: correctness/security; Lens B:
test-quality/doctrine) each ran a full aggressive hunt (not a "were prior findings fixed" check) against
live head 5b74043c83b0e5ec70eaa24f7f2f797ab4c8af80. Both independently reproduced: the 171-class/
712-route inventory, the 38-route reachable-while-locked set, both adversarial mutations (guard revert
-> 16 tests red; controller-append -> 2 tests red), the 399 net LOC figure, and zero net-new banned
casts. Both verdicts: CLEAN. No P0/P1 findings from either lens. P2/P3 findings (aliased-@Controller-
import blind spot in the AST scanner; object/array-form @Controller-argument blind spot; FEATURE_
DUNNING_V2 env-read invisible to the static env scanner; filename-convention-dependent controller
discovery) are real but affect zero controllers in the current tree and are tracked as DUN-1e follow-up,
not merge blockers.

Audit reports: workspace audits/BACKEND_523_LENSA_AUDIT_REPORT.md, BACKEND_523_LENSB_AUDIT_REPORT.md

Mount DunningLockoutGuard as the final global APP_GUARD (after JwtAuthGuard) so
the Day-10 hard lockout is enforced on real HTTP traffic. The guard preserves
its self-gating (HARD no-op while FEATURE_DUNNING_V2 is OFF) and fail-open
semantics, and bypasses billing/checkout/payment-recovery/auth/health plus the
dedicated Roman chat surface (/roman/*).

Scope the lockout carve-out to /roman/* only: the entitlement-gated student
assistant surface stays LOCKED, while the dedicated Roman chat stays reachable so
Roman can explain the lockout. Document that the @Optional VoicePolicyService
resolves (VoiceModule is @Global) so lockout_copy is computed, but the global
HttpExceptionFilter envelope drops it, so the client 403 contract is exactly
code + message. FEATURE_DUNNING_V2 is NOT flipped.

Add unit and over-the-wire e2e coverage: flag OFF is a no-op; a locked user gets
403 LOCKED_DUNNING on protected routes; unlocked users pass; billing/auth/health
are not bricked; /roman/sessions is reachable while locked; the student chat
stays 403; the 403 envelope carries code + message but not lockout_copy.

head_commit.message:
fix(dunning-v2): match the lockout allow-list on full route prefixes, not segment position

The Day-10 lockout allow-list admitted any path whose FIRST OR SECOND segment
was one of eight tokens. Two consequences, both found by the P0-AUDIT of
5076a07a and both fixed here:

- `scheduling/auth/google/initiate` and `/callback` were reachable while
  locked out, because their second segment is `auth`. Google Calendar OAuth
  is a paid integration surface, not payment recovery, so this was a bypass
  of the guard's only security property (Lens A P1-1). The leak was generic:
  any future controller with a colliding second segment inherited it.
- The carve-out the positional clause was written for missed the v1 coach
  billing surface. `coach/me/billing` and `coach/me/billing/portal-session`
  were LOCKED while the mobile `coach/billing/*` variant of the same
  BillingService capability stayed open — locking a delinquent coach out of
  the Stripe portal they need to cure the delinquency (Lens A P2-1).

The positional clause is replaced by an explicit list of full normalized
route prefixes. Reachability is unchanged for every other route.

Lens B P1-2 recorded that the existing 47 cases assert the allow-list against
hand-picked example paths, never the mounted route table, which is why P1-1
survived review. The new spec enumerates all 161 controllers and 712 mounted
routes and asserts the EXACT reachable-while-locked set, so a new controller
cannot silently inherit an exemption.

Baseline: 5076a07a1e54b14e3db84d3aa128fb0bb44542d7
FEATURE_DUNNING_V2 remains default-OFF; no flag is flipped.

head_commit.message:
fix(importer): include entity_type in ScoutIngestEntity idempotency key (P0 silent loss)

The key shipped by 20261222000000 is UNIQUE (coach_id, intent_id, source_id),
but entity_type is part of the ingest envelope and stored only as a value. The
extension posts one envelope per entity_type within a single intent, and
source ids are namespaced by type at every adapter we model (a TrueCoach
client and a TrueCoach workout can both be "1042"). The second envelope of a
crawl session therefore collided with the first and was dropped.

The drop is silent, which makes this P0 rather than P1. The writer is
createMany({ skipDuplicates: true }) -- INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING --
which never raises P2002. The row simply never lands, and the caller's
`deduped = received - count` then reports the lost entity as a successful
replay. A crawl reports success while discarding an entire entity_type.

Restates R-IDEMP-1 (2026-07-08) rather than replacing it: captured_at stays a
value (a re-observation within an intent must remain a no-op replay), and
entity_type becomes a key column (the unit of identity is "the coach saw
entity X of type T during crawl session Y"). The corrected key matches the two
sibling scout tables that already got this right.

Widening a unique key cannot fail on existing data: every row satisfying
UNIQUE (a,b,c) satisfies UNIQUE (a,b,c,d). No backfill, no data rewrite, no
constraint-violation abort -- purely permissive. 20261222000000 is shipped and
is not edited (ENGINEERING_RULES 2, append-only); its stale header stands as
historical record (R5).

Reversibility (R82/R106): companion down.sql restores the narrow key. The
reverse is narrowing and will abort if rows only the widened key permits
already exist -- correct behaviour, not a defect: it refuses rather than
deleting a coach's crawl data. Both directions are exercised as a dry-run.

  index swap. Gated on SCOUT_INGEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL with a loud skip (R69).

head_commit.message:
fix(dunning-v2): scope lockout carve-out to /roman/*, correct mount docs

The lockout allow-list carved out the entitlement-gated student assistant
routes (a paid value surface) while blocking /roman/*, the dedicated Roman
chat that must stay reachable so Roman can explain the lockout. Narrow
ROMAN_CHAT_PREFIXES to ['roman'] so the student assistant surface stays
LOCKED and the actual Roman explanation surface is allowed. The
billing/auth/health carve-outs are unchanged.

Correct the AppModule mount comment: the guard's @Optional VoicePolicyService
DOES resolve (VoiceModule is @Global), so lockout_copy is computed when the
flag is ON, but the global HttpExceptionFilter envelope drops it. The
client-visible 403 contract is therefore exactly code + message. Delivering
lockout_copy would need an envelope change, tracked as a separate pre-flip gap.

and /roman/* is allowed; e2e proves over the wire that /roman/sessions returns
200, the student chat stays 403 LOCKED_DUNNING, and the 403 envelope carries
code + message but NOT lockout_copy.

head_commit.message:
feat(dunning-v2): enforce Day-10 lockout by mounting guard in global chain

Register DunningLockoutGuard as a global APP_GUARD in app.module, after
JwtAuthGuard, so the B3 Smart Dunning v2 hard-lockout is actually enforced
on real traffic instead of only being available for opt-in @UseGuards.

Ordering is load-bearing: the guard resolves the caller's DunningState by
req.user.id, and defensively no-ops when identity is absent, so it must run
after authentication. Placed last so req.user is populated first (APP_GUARD
execution follows provider registration order, the same guarantee the
existing JwtAuthGuard-before-UserThrottlerGuard ordering relies on).

The guard's existing posture is unchanged: HARD no-op while FEATURE_DUNNING_V2
is OFF, fails OPEN on lookup errors, and bypasses billing/auth/health/Roman-chat
via its internal allow-list — so global mounting ahead of the operator flip
cannot brick public/health/auth traffic or the recovery surface. Adds an
HTTP-level e2e proving flag-OFF no-op, LOCKED_DUNNING 403 for an eligible
locked client, unlocked pass-through, carve-out routes stay reachable, and
that the guard receives the authenticated identity.

head_commit.message:
chore(prod-readiness): register Scout/importer flags default-OFF (R-SCOUT-READINESS-1)

Register FEATURE_SCOUT_INGEST, FEATURE_SCOUT_RECONSTRUCT and
FEATURE_EXTENSION_PAIRING in the prod-readiness registry as explicit
default-OFF (tier: feature, prod_default: OFF, auto_flip_on_in_prod: false,
owner: importer), add FEATURE_EXTENSION_PAIRING=false to .env.example, and add
one deploy-readiness assertion proving all three are registered default-OFF.

The three flags are already live route gates in src/ (feature-flag middleware
reads them via process.env[route.envVar]); this slice only closes the
registry/env/test registration gap. Config + test only; no runtime or src
change; all flags remain default-OFF.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(prod-readiness): correct branch-protection guidance for deploy-readiness checks

head_commit.message:
fix(prod-readiness): correct branch-protection guidance for deploy-readiness checks

deploy-readiness-gate runs only on workflow_dispatch and push to release/*,
never on pull_request. Recommending it as a branch-protection required check
leaves a check that never reports on PRs, permanently blocking every merge to
main (the script's own canonical rule). Correct the runbook and the workflow
header comment so they never recommend it as a required PR check, and clearly
distinguish it from the PR-eligible test-deploy-readiness check.

Add test-deploy-readiness (pull_request, no paths filter; stable check context)
to the canonical REQUIRED_CHECKS list in setup-branch-protection.sh, and record
deploy-readiness-gate in the explicit not-PR-eligible exclusion note.

No repository settings changed; the script is not run here. Strict gate,
runtime behavior, workflow triggers, and importer flags are untouched.
